clue.text: Prepare to shoot back, but for being in drinking venue

parts.note: you cock a gun before firing it
the tail is the back end of something
bar means except, as in 'bar none'

explanation.surface: A gunman readies himself to return fire, but only if he is not stuck in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'But for' reads as a conjunction, yet it is the preposition 'bar', meaning except. The enumeration's comma marks where the two words split.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocktail bar is a type of establishment where people go to buy and consume mixed alcoholic beverages.

clue.text: Conservative articles Liberal plugged for monstrous figure

indicators.note: a plugged hole has something stuffed inside it, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: the indefinite articles a and an

explanation.surface: Conservative newspaper pieces stuffed with a Liberal viewpoint are seen as something monstrous.
explanation.walkthrough: The two articles are A and AN, and the Liberal sits between them rather than after them. Caliban is the misshapen creature in Shakespeare's The Tempest.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's savage, deformed slave on Prospero's island is literature's best-known beastly creature, fitting the description.

clue.text: Radiation pioneer finding iodine in salt

indicators.note: the plain preposition places one piece inside another

parts.note: to salt meat or fish is to cure it

explanation.surface: A scientist discovers iodine in table salt, which is true of iodised salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' looks like a noun but works as the verb meaning to preserve, which is CURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Marie Curie did groundbreaking research into radioactivity, winning two Nobel prizes for the work.

clue.text: Curtailed period without reason, without courage

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short at the tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to do something idly is to do it without any real reason or purpose

explanation.surface: Someone apologising for a shortened session for no good reason, sounding faint-hearted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without reason' sits beside 'period' as if describing it, but it is a separate piece meaning aimlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting timidly means acting with fear and a lack of boldness, which is to say without courage.

clue.text: Evil couple, with only one in court regarding criminal behaviour

parts.note: ill means evil, as in ill deeds

indicators.note: with only means just a single letter of the pair is kept at this point

parts.note: a couple of ones, written as two letter Is

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the court abbreviation

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I, the other of the pair

explanation.surface: A wicked pair, only one of whom ends up in the dock for criminal acts.
explanation.walkthrough: The couple is a pair of Roman ones: one stands beside the evil word and only the other goes into court.
explanation.definitionFit: Illicit means forbidden by law, so it describes conduct that is unlawful or criminal.

clue.text: Report learning about American Indian city

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is surrounded

parts.note: a report is the sound of a gunshot or explosion

explanation.surface: A paper on education in the United States, set beside a city in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' sounds like a document, but it is the noise of a gun, BANG. The A slips in at the join between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Bangalore, now officially Bengaluru, is the capital of Karnataka and India's technology hub.

clue.text: Difficulty with seventh lot of wine generating friction

parts.note: wines are stored and listed by bin
G is the seventh letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Trouble with the seventh batch of wine causes arguments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seventh' is not an ordinal attached to the lot but the seventh letter, G, which goes on the end. A bin is a numbered wine rack or batch in a cellar.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbing is the action of surfaces moving against each other, which is what friction means physically.

clue.text: Pivotal point not all complete — bit brief?

indicators.note: not all means one letter is left off the end of the word
brief means shortened, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a crumb is a small bit

explanation.surface: Asking whether a short bit is the incomplete key point of an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: FULL drops its last L to give FUL, and CRUMB drops its B to give CRUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A fulcrum is the support on which a lever turns, the point on which something pivots.

clue.text: The hard life sadly driving daughter away, to adopt a fringe practitioner

indicators.note: something sadly done is badly done, so the letters are knocked out of order
driving something off removes it from the group
away means gone, completing the instruction to take something out

parts.note: the fodder takes in the letter A

explanation.surface: A parent's tough existence drives their daughter out, so they take in someone offbeat.
explanation.walkthrough: Take D out of THE HARD LIFE, add A, and rearrange all eleven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A faith healer claims to cure illness through prayer or belief, an alternative therapy outside mainstream medicine.

clue.text: It's often made of yew or pine wood? Not entirely

parts.note: to pine for something is to long for it

indicators.note: not entirely means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: in the game of bowls a bowl is also called a wood

explanation.surface: A question about whether an item is made of yew or pine timber, half answered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pine wood' looks like a type of timber but splits into a verb and a term from the game of bowls.
explanation.definitionFit: The English longbow was traditionally carved from yew, the classic medieval archery weapon.

clue.text: Turn by air, securing sources of reliable basic electric current? That's how I work

definitions.text: Turn by air, securing sources of reliable basic electric current? That's how I work

indicators.note: by means beside, so the pieces are placed next to each other

parts.note: to wind is to turn, as with a handle

indicators.note: to secure is to hold firmly, so one piece holds others
a source is where something begins, so first letters are taken

parts.note: the opening letters of these two words
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A generator describes itself: turned by moving air, it provides dependable electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the answer is speaking in 'That's how I work'. TUNE holds R, B and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Blades spun by moving air drive a generator, producing power, which is exactly how such a machine operates.

clue.text: Inspire announcement of personal sorrow after student leaves

indicators.note: whatever leaves is taken away

parts.note: saying 'I'm blue' declares that you are sad

explanation.surface: A pupil departs, and someone confesses their grief in a moving way.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is I'M BLUE, apostrophe dropped; the student is L, as on a learner driver's plate.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbue someone is to fill them with a feeling or quality, much as inspiring them does.

clue.text: Detective and prisoner accepting rubbish given by one delivering sentences?

indicators.note: given alongside means placed next to
to accept is to take in, so one piece receives another

explanation.surface: A detective and a convict take in rubbish from a judge handing out prison terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One delivering sentences' suggests a judge, but the sentences are spoken for someone to write down; 'one' also supplies I in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Dictation is speaking words aloud for another person to transcribe, i.e. handing over sentences by voice.

clue.text: Quick to have one replacing America's candour

indicators.note: replacing means one thing takes another's place

parts.note: A for America, the letter swapped out

explanation.surface: A demand for speed takes the place of American frankness.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the A in HASTY for ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Candour and honesty are synonyms: both mean frankness and truthfulness in speaking.

clue.text: Poor sci-fi, after editing? Dull

indicators.note: editing reworks text, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bad science-fiction script, even once revised, is still boring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' looks like a verdict on quality, but it is simply fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Soporific means sleep-inducing, and something tedious enough to send you to sleep is boring.

clue.text: Beginning to tremble after admitting small amount

indicators.note: after says which piece comes later in the answer
a beginning is the opening letter of a word

explanation.surface: Someone starts to shake after confessing a tiny sum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Admitting' looks like a container indicator, but it is the word THOUGH, as in 'though I admit'.
explanation.definitionFit: A thought can mean a tiny bit, as in 'a thought too salty', meaning slightly.

clue.text: Avoids predicament, heading away when rounding headland

indicators.note: rounding means going around, so the shortened word surrounds the headland
heading away means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a mess is a predicament, a difficult situation

explanation.surface: A sailor dodges trouble by steering round a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headland' sounds like part of the same instruction as 'heading away', but it is the piece being rounded.
explanation.definitionFit: To escape a thing is to evade or get away from it, which is what avoiding it means.

clue.text: One wouldn't need binoculars to see policemen around Yard receiving tips from criminal

indicators.note: around means the police word surrounds the rest
receiving tips from means the yard letter takes on the two ends of the next word, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Police surround a yard where a criminal is caught, with no need for field glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: The tips of criminal are its first and last letters; the police word goes round the yard letter and those tips.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cyclops is a one-eyed giant of Greek myth, so a pair of eyepieces would be useless to him.

clue.text: Old African state in southern area — or eastern area?

indicators.note: the plain preposition places one piece inside another

explanation.surface: A question of geography: is a former African nation in the south of the continent or the east?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old African state' reads as the definition, but it is O plus MALI; the real definition is the tentative 'eastern area?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Somalia occupies the Horn of Africa on the continent's easterly coast, an example of a region there.

clue.text: Airman's first to board smart chopper

indicators.note: to board a vehicle is to go inside it
first picks out the opening letter of a word

explanation.surface: A pilot is the first to climb into a sleek helicopter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopper' invites a helicopter, but it is the butcher's blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleaver is a heavy knife used by butchers for hacking through meat and bone.

clue.text: Claim Cu transmuted into another metal

indicators.note: to transmute is to change form, so the letters change order

explanation.surface: An alchemist boasts that copper, symbol Cu, has been turned into a different element.
explanation.walkthrough: Cu is copper's chemical symbol, which makes 'another metal' fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Calcium is a soft alkaline earth element, chemically classed among the metals like copper.

clue.text: What makes Vera stoop in US?

definitions.text: What makes Vera stoop in US?

parts.words: What makes Vera stoop in US
parts.note: the surface asks what causes a woman called Vera to bend down; the setter's reading: the answer starts with her name, and it is what Americans call a stoop, a raised porch

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stoop' looks like a verb about bending; in American English a stoop is the porch or steps at a house front. Add a few letters to VERA and you have one.
explanation.definitionFit: A veranda is a roofed platform along a house front, the same as an American stoop or porch.

clue.text: Lady's initial charm lay in disposition of tears

indicators.note: an initial is the first letter of a name
a disposition is an arrangement, so the letters are set out anew

explanation.surface: A woman's early appeal lay in her tendency to weep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disposition' reads as temperament, but here it means arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Lachrymal is the adjective for things connected with weeping, as in the lachrymal glands.

clue.text: Exclamation of surprise — gin running short (Queen's favourite?)

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: running short means the word is cut off before its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in shock that the gin is running out, a royal tipple.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen Elizabeth II was famous for keeping corgis, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The late Queen's best-known pets were Pembroke Welsh corgis, so the breed is her favourite by example.

clue.text: Something regurgitated about religious deity

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: cud is food a cow brings back up to chew

explanation.surface: A religious idol is compared to something coughed back up.
explanation.walkthrough: PI, short for pious, is a crossword staple for religious.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupid is the Roman god of love, a divine figure from classical mythology.

clue.text: Not too many people perhaps backing low force in control? Not quite

indicators.note: in places these pieces within the shortened control word
not quite means the word loses its final letter
backing means read in reverse

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
F is the physics abbreviation for force

explanation.surface: A modest crowd, perhaps, supporting a weak force that isn't quite in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' is the verb for what cattle do, not an adjective; 'Not quite' trims the word for control.
explanation.definitionFit: A roomful is as many as fit in one room, which is a modest number of people, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Send packet in time, missing post's latest strike

indicators.note: the plain preposition places one piece inside another
whatever is missing has been taken out
the latest part of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the word time with the T gone
the final letter of post, which is removed
a ping sends a test packet across a network

explanation.surface: Get the parcel off promptly, because the postal workers' walkout is coming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Packet' suggests a parcel, but it is a data packet; 'post's latest' is the T at the end of post, which comes out of TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: To impinge on something is to collide with or hit it, the older physical sense of the verb.

clue.text: Very well — I start to admit — after medical trips seen in selfies and posts?

indicators.note: after says which piece comes later in the answer
something that trips stumbles, so the letters fall out of order
a start is the opening letter of a word

explanation.surface: A patient concedes that hospital visits show up in their online photos and updates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trips' reads as journeys but is the anagram signal. 'Very well' is SO in the sense of 'so be it', a grudging agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Selfies and posts are the typical content of Instagram and Facebook, so the definition works by example.
